item.title: 2026 Goombay — Sat Sep 12, 10:00 AM — YMI Cultural Center/Pack Square Park
item.description:
Goombay Festival returns to Asheville’s historic East End for a vibrant celebration of Black culture, music, food, art, and community! Rooted in the rich traditions of Asheville’s Black community, Goombay brings neighbors and visitors together for a weekend of unforgettable experiences—from live music and Go-Go to local vendors, art, dance, food, family activities, and the Ujima 5K. Presented by the YMI Cultural Center, Goombay is more than a festival—it is a celebration of heritage, resilience, creativity, and the people who continue to shape Western North Carolina. Come experience the energy, support Black-owned businesses and artists, reconnect with community, and celebrate the legacy of Asheville’s historic East End. Come for the culture. Stay for the community. Leave with the Goombay spirit. ymiculturalcenter.org/goombay
Saturday Music Lineup:

item.title: Ledford Gap/Powhatan Loop: 7 mi., 1,100 ft. elev. — Fri Sep 18, 9:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **[RSVP opens Sunday, Sept. 13th, 8:00 pm]**
With so many trail segments cobbled together, this is practically a grand tour of the Bent Creek area! We'll start at the Ledford Branch parking lot and cover parts of Bent Creek Gap Rd., Explorer Loop Trail, Sleepy Gap Trail, Shut-in Trail, Deerfield Connector, Small Creek Trail, Homestead Trail, Hard Times Rd., and Deer Lake Lodge Trail. (There are a few other unnamed segments as well.) Total distance is around 6.5 miles with an elevation gain of just under 1,100'. We'll do a moderate pace of around 2.4 mph. It's not an easy hike for many of us. I'd give it a 4 out of 10, while many of my other hikes are in the 2 - 3.5 range with half the elevation gain.
Wear sensible hiking footwear, and bring an ample water supply. Around 2/3 of the way through, we'll find a spot for a short snack break.

item.description:
Birding for Beginners with Shane Myers Tuesday, October 6 | 9 – 10:30am BRN – Elective Register Here!
Join us on this birding walk around the NC Arboretum gardens and trails in search of our most colorful residents. We will go over best practices for using binoculars, recommendations for purchasing your own binoculars, and popular field guides to use. Bring your own binoculars but if you do not have a pair we have some loaner binoculars available to use during the program. This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.
